title: Rigveda 10.126: To all the gods
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (1711 CE (colophon: Saṃvat 1768)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 10.126: To all the gods: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of a 1711 Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 10.126 is a hymn of 8 verses addressed to all the gods. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 10, the last and latest book. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (University of Pennsylvania), a paper manuscript of the eighth aṣṭaka (RV 10.46-10.191) of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā in Devanāgarī, 158 leaves, 6 lines to the page, with the accents marked in red; the scribe's colophon on fol. 158 gives Saṃvat 1768 (1711 CE); this hymn stands on fol. 113r-113v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Like most Rigveda manuscripts, Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 writes a repeated refrain in short form after its first occurrence (for example kasmai° for kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema); the Sanskrit shown is the full text of Aufrecht's edition.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).

translation.original_ref: RV 10.126.1-3 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 7, varga 13); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 113r
translation.original_text:
1na tam aṁho̱ na du̍ri̱taṁ devā̍so aṣṭa̱ martya̍m | sa̱joṣa̍so̱ yam a̍rya̱mā mi̱tro naya̍nti̱ varu̍ṇo̱ ati̱ dviṣa̍ḥ ||
2tad dhi va̱yaṁ vṛ̍ṇī̱mahe̱ varu̍ṇa̱ mitrārya̍man | yenā̱ nir aṁha̍so yū̱yam pā̱tha ne̱thā ca̱ martya̱m ati̱ dviṣa̍ḥ ||
3te nū̱naṁ no̱ 'yam ū̱taye̱ varu̍ṇo mi̱tro a̍rya̱mā | nayi̍ṣṭhā u no ne̱ṣaṇi̱ parṣi̍ṣṭhā u naḥ pa̱rṣaṇy ati̱ dviṣa̍ḥ ||
translation.text:
1No peril, no severe distress, ye Gods, affects the mortal man, Whom Aryaman and Mitra lead, and Varuṇa, of one accord, beyond his foes.
2This very thing do we desire, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, Whereby ye guard the mortal man from sore distress, and lead him safe beyond his foes.
3These are, each one, our present helps, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman. Best leaders, best deliverers to lead us on and bear as safe beyond our foes.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 113r (OPenn image 112, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.125.7 ‹-asya mūrdhan mama yonir›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 113v, begins in RV 10.126.4 ‹-yuṣmākaṁ śarmaṇi priye syāma›. Verses 10.126.1-3 end on this page.

translation.original_ref: RV 10.126.4-8 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 7, varga 13); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 113v
translation.original_text:
4yū̱yaṁ viśva̱m pari̍ pātha̱ varu̍ṇo mi̱tro a̍rya̱mā | yu̱ṣmāka̱ṁ śarma̍ṇi pri̱ye syāma̍ supraṇīta̱yo 'ti̱ dviṣa̍ḥ ||
5ā̱di̱tyāso̱ ati̱ sridho̱ varu̍ṇo mi̱tro a̍rya̱mā | u̱gram ma̱rudbhī̍ ru̱draṁ hu̍ve̱mendra̍m a̱gniṁ sva̱staye 'ti̱ dviṣa̍ḥ ||
6netā̍ra ū̱ ṣu ṇa̍s ti̱ro varu̍ṇo mi̱tro a̍rya̱mā | ati̱ viśvā̍ni duri̱tā rājā̍naś carṣaṇī̱nām ati̱ dviṣa̍ḥ ||
7śu̱nam a̱smabhya̍m ū̱taye̱ varu̍ṇo mi̱tro a̍rya̱mā | śarma̍ yacchantu sa̱pratha̍ ādi̱tyāso̱ yad īma̍he̱ ati̱ dviṣa̍ḥ ||
8yathā̍ ha̱ tyad va̍savo gau̱rya̍ṁ cit pa̱di ṣi̱tām amu̍ñcatā yajatrāḥ | e̱vo ṣv a1̱̍sman mu̍ñcatā̱ vy aṁha̱ḥ pra tā̍ry agne prata̱raṁ na̱ āyu̍ḥ ||
translation.text:
4Ye compass round and guard each man, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman: In your dear keeping may we be, ye who are excellent as guides beyond our foes.
5Âdityas are beyond all foes,– Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman: Strong Rudra with the Marut host, Indra, Agni let us call for weal beyond our foes.
6These lead us safely over all, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, These who are Kings of living men, over all troubles far away beyond our foes.
7May they give bliss to aid us well, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman: May the Âdityas, when we pray, grant us wide shelter and defence beyond our foes.
8As in this place, O Holy Ones, ye Vasus freed even the Gaud when her feet were fettered. So free us now from trouble and affliction: and let our life be lengthened still, O Api.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 113v (OPenn image 113, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.126.4 ‹-yuṣmākaṁ śarmaṇi priye syāma›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 114r, begins in RV 10.127.1 ‹viśvā adhi śriyo 'dhita›. Verses 10.126.4-8 end on this page; 10.126.4 begins on fol. 113r.
